MOUTH SYMPTOMS
1Common allergens include medication, food or insect bite/sting within the past few hours. 2Add 2.5mL (½ teaspoon) of table salt to 200mL lukewarm water.

Approach to the patient with mouth symptoms not needing urgent attention • If on abacavir, check for abacavir hypersensitivity reaction (AHR) 131. If swelling of lips 49. If gum or tooth problem 54. • Ask about dry mouth. Wear a mask while examining the mouth and check for redness, white patches, blisters, ulcers or cracks:
White patches on cheeks, gums, tongue, palate

© Ourania Nicolatou-Galitis et al (CC BY-SA 4.0). Oral thrush/candida likely • Give nystatin suspension 100 000IU/mL (1mL) 6 hourly after meal for 7 days. Keep inside mouth as long as possible. Continue for 2 days after white patches resolved. • If on inhaled corticosteroids, advise to rinse mouth with water after use. • Test for HIV 124 and diabetes 19. • If patient has a life-limiting illness, also give palliative care 191.
If difficulty or pain on swallowing,
oesophageal candida likely: • Give fluconazole 200mg daily for 14 days. • Test for HIV 124. If HIV positive, start ART 126. • If no better, refer.
Red, cracked corners of mouth
© Dr Richard Ashton: dermnetnz.org

Angular cheilitis/stomatitis likely • Apply zinc and castor oil ointment 8 hourly. • If patient also has oral candida, treat as in adjacent column and apply clotrimazole cream 12 hourly for 2 weeks. • If crusts and blisters around mouth, impetigo likely 93. • If very itchy, contact dermatitis likely. Identify and remove irritant. • If dentures, ensure good fit and advise to clean every night. • If on inhaled corticosteroids, advise to rinse mouth after use. • If no better or uncertain of cause: - Check Hb. If < 12g/dL (woman) or < 13g/dL
(man), anaemia likely 44. - Test for HIV 124 and diabetes 19. - If still uncertain, refer.
Painful blisters on lips/mouth
© Dr Mashihul Hossain

Herpes simplex likely • Test for HIV 124. • Advise to rinse mouth with salt water2 for one minute twice a day. • Apply petroleum jelly to blisters on lips. • For pain, give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • If extensive, apply tetracaine 0.5% gel to blisters 6 hourly. • If HIV, give aciclovir 400mg 8 hourly for 7 days. • If severe or no better after 1 week of treatment, refer.
Painful ulcer/s with central white patch
© Florian Brandt
Aphthous ulcer/s likely • Apply tetracaine 0.5% gel on ulcers 6 hourly. • Refer if: - Ulcer > 1cm - Not healed within
10 days.
Advise to avoid spicy, hot, sticky, dry or acidic food and to eat soft, moist food. Keep mouth and teeth clean by brushing and rinsing regularly.
Dry mouth

• If thirst, urinary frequency, weight loss, check for diabetes 19. • If runny or blocked nose 51. • Look for and treat oral candida (see adjacent). • Review medication: furosemide, amitriptyline, chlorphenamine, antipsychotics and morphine can cause dry mouth. Discuss with doctor. • Advise to sip fluids frequently. Sucking on oranges, pineapple, lemon or passion fruit may help. • If patient has a life- limiting illness, also give palliative care 191.
